items.title: Can Share Buybacks Continue to Prop Up Toro Stock?
items.summary: Toro (TTC) trades within about 4% of its 52-week high, and it keeps buying back shares with cash from zero-turn mowers, golf equipment and Ditch Witch drills. But over three years the buybacks have only softened a fall in earnings per share, and today's price assumes profit growth comes back.

items.title: Trump and Xi Buy Time on Trade. Farm and Chip Stocks Are Watching Closely.
items.summary: The U.S. and China extended their trade truce, but the deal treated soybeans and semiconductors very differently. Which sector actually has something to gain, and which is already priced as if China does not exist?

items.title: Is Deere (DE) Stock Reasonable After Its Strong Q2 Beat?
items.summary: Deere has delivered a powerful run in recent years, and the stock now trades near the upper end of its recent range, which naturally puts the spotlight on what investors are paying for its underlying cash flows. With that share price backdrop in mind, the question is how closely the current valuation lines up with the stream of cash the business is expected to generate over time. items.title: 2 Industrials Stocks Worth Investigating and 1 Facing Challenges
items.summary: Whether you see them or not, industrials businesses play a crucial part in our daily activities. Still, their generally high capital requirements expose them to the ups and downs of economic cycles, and the market seems confused about where we could go next. This uncertainty has led to a flat return for the industry over the past six months while the S&P 500 was up 16.9%.

items.title: What Would You Have Needed To Notice In Caterpillar Stock?
items.summary: Caterpillar (CAT) stock returned 74% in the twelve months to September 23, 2026. A $10,000 holding at the start was worth about $17,350 at the end. The run turned out to be about customers buying more, led by power equipment for data centers. Caterpillar's own sales, though, were still falling when the run began. You would have needed a public sign that Caterpillar's demand was turning before its sales did.

items.title: Don’t expect a grand bargain from the Trump-Xi summit: Yardeni
items.summary: Investing.com -- Yardeni Research has cautioned investors not to expect a major breakthrough when President Trump meets Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday, though it said modest progress would still be welcome.

items.title: 1 Profitable Stock to Research Further and 2 We Find Risky
items.summary: Even if a company is profitable, it doesn’t always mean it’s a great investment. Some struggle to maintain growth, face looming threats, or fail to reinvest wisely, limiting their future potential.

items.title: 1 Large-Cap Stock with Promising Prospects and 2 We Turn Down
items.summary: Large-cap stocks usually command their industries because they have the scale to drive market trends. The flip side though is that their sheer size can limit growth as expanding further becomes an increasingly challenging task.
